name: JavaScript
summary: Learn JavaScript syntax, collections, promises, browser APIs, and local Node.js modules.

lessons.title: Values, bindings, and comparisons
lessons.explanation: Use const when a binding will keep referring to the same value and let when you intend to reassign it. JavaScript has primitives such as number, string, Boolean, undefined, and null, as well as objects. Use strict comparisons to avoid implicit conversions.

api.name: console.log(...)
api.description: Write values to the developer console or terminal.

api.name: Number(text)
api.description: Convert a value to a number. Invalid numeric text produces NaN.

api.name: Number.isFinite(value)
api.description: Check for a finite number without converting its type.

lessons.practice: Read three values as strings and print only the ones that convert to finite numbers.
lessons.pitfall: const prevents reassignment of a binding. Properties of its object can still change.

exercise.expected: Convert input strings to finite numbers before using them.
exercise.completion: Reject invalid text and decide explicitly how to handle an empty string.

lessons.title: Branches, loops, and functions
lessons.explanation: Functions receive inputs and return values. Arrow functions are concise for callbacks. Use for...of to iterate over values from an array or another iterable.

api.name: function name(...)
api.description: Declare a reusable operation.

api.name: (value) => expression
api.description: Write a function that returns the expression.

api.name: return value
api.description: End the current function and hand a result to the caller.

lessons.practice: Read a line of space-separated integers from stdin. Sum only the odd values.
lessons.pitfall: for...in iterates enumerable property keys. Use for...of when you need the values of an iterable.

exercise.expected: Print the sum as one integer. Treat an empty line as an empty array.
exercise.completion: Include negative odd values, an all-even list, and an empty line.

lessons.title: Arrays, objects, maps, and sets
lessons.explanation: Use arrays for ordered items, objects for named fields, Map for dynamic keys of any type, and Set for unique values. Array methods can express a transformation without manual indexing.

api.name: Array.map() / Array.filter()
api.description: Transform every item or keep items matching a condition.

api.name: Array.reduce()
api.description: Combine items into a result. Provide an initial value for an empty input.

api.name: Map.set() / Map.get()
api.description: Set or read a key-value entry.

api.name: Set.add() / Set.has()
api.description: Add a unique value or test membership.

lessons.practice: Group minutes by category in a Map. Display each category total.
lessons.pitfall: Array.sort mutates the array and compares strings by default. Use a comparator for numbers.

exercise.expected: Compute total minutes for a chosen activity.
exercise.completion: An absent activity returns zero and the original rows are still available.

lessons.title: Object access, defaults, and JSON
lessons.explanation: Access object fields with a dot for a fixed name or brackets for a computed name. Optional chaining stops at null or undefined. Nullish coalescing provides a fallback for those same two values.

api.name: JSON.parse(text)
api.description: Decode valid JSON text. Invalid JSON throws SyntaxError.

api.name: JSON.stringify(value)
api.description: Encode data representable by JSON as text.

api.name: Object.entries(object)
api.description: List the own enumerable string-keyed properties as key-value pairs.

lessons.practice: Change the payload to omit profile. Explain why 0 still survives when visits is present.
lessons.pitfall: JSON parsing checks syntax. Validate the shape before trusting fields in external data.

exercise.expected: Keep a saved visits count of zero and provide a default for a missing count.
exercise.completion: An absent profile defaults to one while a profile with zero reports zero.

lessons.title: Promises, async, and error handling
lessons.explanation: A Promise represents an eventual result. It can be pending, fulfilled, or rejected. An async function returns a Promise. Await waits for a result inside that function while the runtime can process other work.

api.name: await promise
api.description: Read a successful result or throw its rejection inside an async function.

api.name: Promise.all(iterable)
api.description: Wait for all successes in input order, or reject if any input rejects.

api.name: try / catch
api.description: Handle exceptions and awaited promise rejections.

lessons.practice: Replace an ID with -1 and observe which branch runs. Compare with Promise.allSettled.
lessons.pitfall: Promise.all rejects early on failure. It does not cancel the other operations.

exercise.expected: Resolve a collection of local promises and report an invalid ID clearly.
exercise.completion: The result is in input order and the invalid ID reaches the catch branch.

lessons.title: Browser DOM and events
lessons.explanation: A browser exposes the page as a tree of elements. Use DOM methods to find or create nodes, and event listeners to react to user actions. Put this script in an HTML file and open it in a browser. Save this as counter.html and open it in a browser. Click once to check the result.
lessons.example:
<button id="count" type="button">Count: 0</button>
<script>
  const button = document.querySelector("#count");
  let count = 0;
  button.addEventListener("click", () => {
    count += 1;
    button.textContent = "Count: " + count;
  });
</script>

api.name: document.querySelector(selector)
api.description: Return the first matching element or null.

api.name: Element.addEventListener(type, listener)
api.description: Register an event handler.

api.name: Node.textContent
api.description: Set plain text without interpreting it as HTML.

lessons.practice: Add a separate reset button that sets the same count back to zero.
lessons.pitfall: Use textContent for user-provided text. innerHTML parses markup.

exercise.expected: Show a click counter in a local HTML document.
exercise.completion: One click changes the button text to Count: 1.

lessons.title: Modules, paths, and files in Node.js
lessons.explanation: A module exposes named functions or values with export and uses import to load dependencies. Node.js provides filesystem and path APIs that are separate from browser JavaScript. Save this example as study.mjs.

api.name: node:fs/promises
api.description: Read and write local files through asynchronous operations.

api.name: path.join(parts...)
api.description: Join path segments using the host system rules.

api.name: node:test
api.description: Run tests with the built-in Node.js test runner.

lessons.practice: Write and read an array of scores. Use a separate function to compute its average.
lessons.pitfall: Code running in a browser does not have access to Node.js filesystem modules.

exercise.expected: Save and read a small JSON record in a temporary directory.
exercise.completion: The record survives the read round trip and the temporary files are cleaned up.

lessons.title: Copy the parts of an object you change
lessons.explanation: Spreading an object creates a new outer object and copies its own enumerable properties. A nested object is still shared unless you copy it too. Build copies along the path you change when keeping the original is part of your program’s contract.

api.name: { ...source }
api.description: Copy own enumerable properties into a new object.

api.name: Object.is(a, b)
api.description: Check whether two values are the same, including object identity.

lessons.practice: Update one item of an array without mutating the array or the original item.
lessons.pitfall: A spread only copies one level. Mutating a shared nested object can unexpectedly affect the original.

exercise.expected: The array, changed record, and any changed nested field have independent identities.
exercise.completion: Verify that the original value is unchanged and that an untouched item can still be shared.

lessons.title: Keep private state in a closure
lessons.explanation: A closure is a function together with access to the surrounding bindings where it was created. Each call to the factory below creates a separate count. The returned function can update that count even after the factory has returned.

api.name: function factory()
api.description: Create a fresh set of local bindings for each call.

api.name: return () => value
api.description: Return a function that can read its enclosing bindings.

lessons.practice: Make two independent trackers with increment and read operations.
lessons.pitfall: A closure sees changes to a captured binding. It is not a frozen snapshot of that binding’s initial value.

exercise.expected: Incrementing one tracker leaves the other tracker unchanged.
exercise.completion: Create two trackers at the same start value and increment just one.

lessons.title: Destructure records and handle missing values
lessons.explanation: Object destructuring gives names to selected properties. A destructuring default applies only when a value is undefined. Use a deliberate null check or nullish coalescing when null should also mean missing. Rest collects the remaining own enumerable properties into a new object.

api.name: { key, ...rest }
api.description: Read a property and collect the remaining own enumerable properties.
Use a fallback only when the left operand is null or undefined.

lessons.practice: Write a function that formats a session with a default duration only when its value is missing.
lessons.pitfall: Using || for a default also replaces meaningful values such as zero, false, and an empty string.

exercise.expected: A supplied zero remains zero. A missing duration gets the fallback.
exercise.completion: Test absent, null, zero, and ordinary positive durations.

lessons.title: Sort numbers without changing the source
lessons.explanation: Array.sort mutates its array. With no comparison function it sorts ordinary numeric values as strings, so 10 can precede 2. Copy the array first and pass a comparison for finite numbers.

api.name: array.sort(compare)
api.description: Sort the array in place using the supplied ordering.

api.name: [...array]
api.description: Create a shallow array copy before sorting.

lessons.practice: Sort readings numerically from largest to smallest while keeping the original order available.
lessons.pitfall: If data can contain NaN, reject it or define where it should sort. A comparator should describe a consistent order.

exercise.expected: Duplicates stay in the result and the source array is unchanged.
exercise.completion: Use an empty array, repeated values, and two values whose numeric and text ordering differ.

lessons.title: Export and reuse a function from an ES module
lessons.explanation: ES modules provide explicit imports and exports. An .mjs file tells Node.js to load it as a module regardless of nearby package configuration. This file exports one function and runs a small demonstration. To create a separate caller, import the function from its file using a relative specifier with the extension.

api.name: export function
api.description: Make a named function available to importing modules.

api.name: import { label } from "./lesson.mjs"
api.description: Read the named export from a separate local module.

lessons.practice: Split the function and demonstration into two .mjs files and import the function from the demonstration.
lessons.pitfall: Importing executes a module’s top-level code. Move the demo call into the separate caller to keep the reusable module free of side effects.

exercise.expected: The caller prints the expected label once and the helper prints nothing on its own.
exercise.completion: Run the helper directly and then run the caller with Node.

lessons.title: Keep successful results when a batch partly fails
lessons.explanation: Promise.allSettled waits for every input promise to settle and reports a status for each input, in input order. Use it when a single failure should not discard the other results. Read value only from a fulfilled outcome and reason only from a rejected one.

api.name: Promise.allSettled()
api.description: Collect all outcomes without failing the batch on the first rejected input.

api.name: item.status
api.description: Select the matching result shape.

lessons.practice: Build a local batch validator and collect the accepted values and rejection reasons separately.
lessons.pitfall: Settling all outcomes does not cancel work. For operations that support cancellation, pass an abort signal separately.

exercise.expected: Report each rejection and keep every accepted value in its original order.
exercise.completion: Test with all accepted, all rejected, and a mixed input.

lessons.title: Handle a list of buttons with event delegation
lessons.explanation: A click on a descendant normally bubbles to its ancestor. One list listener can find the closest matching button instead of installing a separate listener for every row. Save this example as choices.html and open it in a browser. Click the Practice button to check the output.
lessons.example: Choose a topic

api.name: Element.closest(selector)
api.description: Look from an element toward its ancestors for a match.

api.name: textContent
api.description: Write a text value without treating it as HTML.

lessons.practice: Append a third button after the listener is registered and keep the same listener.
lessons.pitfall: The actual click target can be inside a button. Matching only event.target as the button misses those clicks.

exercise.expected: Clicking the newly added button updates the output, and clicking an unrelated part of the page does not.
exercise.completion: Test a click on an element inside the button and a click on the list’s surrounding whitespace.

lessons.title: Test pure behavior with Node’s built-in assertions
lessons.explanation: A pure function returns a result from its arguments without changing shared state. Test a normal result and an invalid input separately. Node includes a strict assertions module, so this example needs no package installation. Run this file normally with Node.js.

api.name: assert.equal()
api.description: Check strict equality when imported from node:assert/strict.

api.name: assert.throws()
api.description: Run a callback and require a matching exception.

lessons.practice: Add checks for valid minutes, a fraction, and a numeric string.
lessons.pitfall: Writing assert.throws(minutes(-1), RangeError) calls the function before the assertion can inspect the exception.

exercise.completion: Intentionally break one expected value, confirm the program exits unsuccessfully, and restore it.

prerequisites: Know how to save source files.
Use Node.js 22 or newer for terminal examples. Lessons labeled Browser APIs run in a modern browser with local files.
metadata.miniProject: Build an offline reading list. Group items by status, make a view that filters with DOM events, and add tests for invalid entries in the pure list logic. Render user text with textContent.
